steps.title: Onboard the orders table
steps.plain: A data engineer describes the orders table in YAML and merges a pull request. No pipeline code is written.

inputs.user: Asha (data engineer) merges a pull request that onboards the orders table.

config.yaml:
# manifests/shop_db.yaml  (merged by pull request)
source: shop_db
type: postgres
config:
  ingestion.mode: incremental
datasets:
  - name: orders
    schema: public
    table: orders
    config:
      landing.format: json
      silver.key: order_id
      silver.history: scd1
      quality.on_bad_row: quarantine
      quality.rules: customer_key not null; amount_inr >= 0
      gold.table: fact_sales
      cost.owner: sales-analytics

steps.title: The loader writes the metadata DB
steps.plain: The loader checks every key against the key registry, then writes the five tables in one transaction.
steps.code:
loader.load("manifests/shop_db.yaml")   # validate keys, then upsert in one transaction
# INSERT INTO source_master / source_config / dataset_master / dataset_config ...

steps.title: The pipeline reads its settings
steps.plain: The pipeline reads one row from dataset_view and merges the settings: platform, then source, then dataset. Note quality.on_bad_row: the platform says 'fail', the dataset overrides it with 'quarantine'.
steps.code:
row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM dataset_view WHERE dataset_name = 'orders'").fetchone()
config = {**platform, **source, **dataset}      # platform < source < dataset
fp = sha256(json.dumps(config, sort_keys=True))[:16]

steps.title: The mover drops a file in landing
steps.plain: The mover copies changed rows from the shop's database into a landing file, untouched. Order 1001 came twice; order 1002 has no customer and a negative amount.
steps.code:
# the mover copied rows changed since the watermark into
landing/shop_db/orders/batch=b-0912/orders_2026-10-27_0900.json

inputs.user: Asha (data engineer) merges a pull request that onboards the orders table.

logs: mover: 3 rows written to landing batch b-0912

steps.title: Landing → bronze
steps.plain: The lander checks the run log (batch b-0912 not seen yet), reads the file, adds four audit columns and appends to bronze in one Delta commit. Bronze keeps everything: strings, the duplicate, the bad row.
steps.code:
if run_log.has_succeeded("orders", "bronze", "b-0912"):
    return 0                                   # seen this batch: add nothing
df = (spark.read.json(files)
        .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())
        .withColumn("_source",   F.lit("shop_db"))
        .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit("b-0912"))
        .withColumn("_file",     F.col("_metadata.file_path")))
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("bronze.orders")
logs: bronze: 3 rows appended to bronze.orders (batch b-0912)

steps.title: Bronze → silver: clean, quarantine, dedupe, MERGE
steps.plain: Types are cast, codes standardised, India time turned into UTC. Order 1002 breaks the contract and goes to quarantine with its reason. The duplicate 1001 collapses to one row. A MERGE on order_id writes silver.
steps.code:
typed = (bronze.filter("_batch_id = 'b-0912'")
  .select(F.col("order_id"),
          F.col("customer").alias("customer_key"),
          F.regexp_replace("amount", ",", "").cast("decimal(12,2)").alias("amount_inr"),
          F.to_utc_timestamp(F.to_timestamp("placed", "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm"), "Asia/Kolkata").alias("placed_at_utc"),
          F.lower(F.trim("status")).alias("status"), "_batch_id"))
bad  = typed.filter("customer_key IS NULL OR amount_inr < 0")      # -> quarantine, with the rule
good = typed.subtract(bad)

w = Window.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy(F.col("placed_at_utc").desc())
latest = good.withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(w)).filter("_rn = 1").drop("_rn")
MERGE INTO silver.orders t USING latest s ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED AND t.row_hash <> s.row_hash THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *

rows: customer_key is required; amount must be >= 0

steps.title: Silver → gold, then reconcile
steps.plain: Gold rebuilds the day's partition from silver. Then reconciliation checks: 2 distinct orders in the source = 1 in silver + 1 in quarantine, and silver's amount equals gold's.
steps.code:

SELECT customer_key, order_id, amount_inr FROM silver.orders
WHERE to_date(placed_at_utc) = '2026-10-27'

# reconcile
source distinct orders = 2  ->  silver 1 + quarantine 1   (must match)
silver amount = gold amount                                (must match)

steps.title: The same file arrives again
steps.plain: A network timeout made the mover send batch b-0912 a second time. This happens in real life all the time.

inputs.user: Nobody did anything: the mover retried after a timeout and re-sent batch b-0912.

logs: mover: batch b-0912 re-sent (retry after a network timeout)

steps.title: Landing → bronze: batch check
steps.plain: The lander looks in the run log first: batch b-0912 already succeeded, so it adds nothing. No Spark job runs at all.
steps.code:
if run_log.has_succeeded("orders", "bronze", "b-0912"):
    return 0                                   # seen this batch: add nothing

steps.title: Bronze → silver: MERGE changes nothing
steps.plain: Even if silver runs again, MERGE on order_id finds the same row with the same hash: 0 rows inserted, 0 updated, so the data is safe. But look at the new commit in silver's _delta_log: Delta still removed one file and wrote a new one, copying the unchanged row. Safe for the data, not free. Filtering unchanged rows out before the MERGE (compare row_hash first) avoids the rewrite.
steps.code:
w = Window.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy(F.col("placed_at_utc").desc())
latest = good.withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(w)).filter("_rn = 1").drop("_rn")
MERGE INTO silver.orders t USING latest s ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED AND t.row_hash <> s.row_hash THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *

steps.title: A naive pipeline, first run
steps.plain: Same file, but a naive pipeline: no batch check in bronze, INSERT instead of MERGE in silver, and bad rows filtered out with a WHERE clause instead of quarantined. The first run looks fine: ₹1,250.
steps.code:
df = spark.read.json(files).withColumn(...audit columns...)
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("bronze.orders")   # no batch check
INSERT INTO silver.orders SELECT ... FROM bronze.orders WHERE _batch_id = 'b-0912'   # INSERT, not MERGE

dashboard.note: ⚠ Looks fine. But order 1002 has already vanished: the naive pipeline filtered it out instead of quarantining it.

logs: naive pipeline: first run of batch b-0912

steps.title: The same file again: revenue doubles
steps.plain: Bronze appends the batch again (6 rows). Silver INSERTs order 1001 a second time. Gold now has two rows for one order and the dashboard says ₹2,500. Only reconciliation against the source notices.
steps.code:
df = spark.read.json(files).withColumn(...audit columns...)
df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("bronze.orders")   # no batch check
INSERT INTO silver.orders SELECT ... FROM bronze.orders WHERE _batch_id = 'b-0912'   # INSERT, not MERGE

dashboard.note: ⚠ 0 quarantined because order 1002 was dropped silently. Two bugs. Order 1001 is counted twice (no batch check, INSERT not MERGE), and order 1002 was dropped by a WHERE clause instead of quarantined. A simple row count passes by coincidence; only reconciling by key catches both. Compare with 'Same file again, our pipeline'.

logs: mover: batch b-0912 re-sent (retry after a network timeout)
naive pipeline: batch b-0912 processed again
row-count check: source 2 unique rows, gold 2 rows -> passes by coincidence (a duplicate hides a dropped row)
reconcile by key: source 2 distinct orders = gold 1 distinct + quarantine 0 -> MISMATCH; gold has 2 rows for 1 order(s) -> duplicate key; revenue ₹2,500
